extracted.intended_audience: EPO examiners acting as International Searching Authority (ISA); patent attorneys and applicants interacting with the EPO in the PCT phase
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for performing the international search, preparing the international search report (ISR) and WO-ISA (written opinion) when the EPO acts as International Searching Authority under the PCT, including procedural, substantive and reporting standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective of the search
rubrics_metrics.description: The objective of the international search is to discover the prior art which is relevant for the purpose of determining novelty and inventive step.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The international search does not differ from a European search in objective. The search should identify prior art relevant for novelty and inventive step (see GL/PCT-EPO B-X, 9).

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope / completeness of the search
rubrics_metrics.description: The International Searching Authority must endeavour to discover as much of the relevant prior art as its facilities permit and must, in any case, consult the documentation specified in the PCT Regulations (Rule 34).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The definition 'as its facilities permit' means the international search scope is equivalent to that of a European search. Consult Rule 34 and ISPE Guidelines 15.18 and 15.20. Search thoroughly and consult the mandatory documentation sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effectiveness and efficiency of the search
rubrics_metrics.description: Searches should be conducted effectively and efficiently.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply Section B-III, 2.2 of the Guidelines for Examination in the EPO mutatis mutandis (see GL/ISPE 15.46-15.47). Balance thoroughness with efficient use of available resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search in analogous fields
rubrics_metrics.description: Search strategy should include analogous technical fields where appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply Section B-III, 2.3 of the Guidelines for Examination in the EPO mutatis mutandis and consider Rules 33.2(b),(c) (GL/ISPE 15.48-15.51).

rubrics_metrics.name: Search on the internet and dating of internet citations
rubrics_metrics.description: Internet sources may be searched; special care must be taken concerning the dating of internet citations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply Section B-III, 2.4 of the EPO Guidelines mutatis mutandis (GL/ISPE 15.56-15.59). See GL/PCT-EPO G-IV, 6.4 for dating internet citations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Follow documentation standards for the search as per the Guidelines for Examination in the EPO (Section B-II, 3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The EPO's Section B-II,3 applies mutatis mutandis. Maintain appropriate records of search sources and search steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search report content
rubrics_metrics.description: An international search report is prepared identifying documents constituting the relevant state of the art; it is accompanied by a written opinion (WO-ISA).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare ISR to identify relevant prior-art documents (see GL/PCT-EPO B-X,9) and include the written opinion (see GL/PCT-EPO B-XI). Ensure ISR and WO-ISA reflect the results and reasoning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time limit for establishing ISR and WO-ISA
rubrics_metrics.description: The time limit is three months from receipt of the search copy by the ISA or nine months from the priority date, whichever occurs later.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practically, establish search and written opinion no later than 16 months from the priority date. Monitor timelines carefully (Art.15, Rule 33).

rubrics_metrics.name: Basis for the search
rubrics_metrics.description: The search is carried out on the basis of the search copy of the application as transmitted to the ISA, subject to permitted corrections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See ISPE Guidelines 15.21 and 15.23. Only obvious mistakes or formal matters contrary to the PCT (called to applicant's attention by RO) may be corrected prior to the search (see GL/PCT-EPO H-IV).

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation of claims (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims should be interpreted for search purposes following the EPO Guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply Section B-III, 3.2 of the Guidelines for Examination mutatis mutandis. Interpret claims to determine the subject-matter to be searched.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims with explicit references to description or drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: If claims contain explicit references to features elucidated in the description or drawings, the examiner should search those features as long as they are unambiguously defined by specific parts of the description.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit references are permissible only where 'absolutely necessary' (cf. GL/PCT-EPO F-IV, 4.17). If reference does not clearly identify which subject-matter is included, the examiner may contact the applicant informally before the search (see GL/PCT-EPO B-VIII, 3.3). For 'omnibus claims' (e.g. 'substantially as herein described') do not request informal clarification and designate the search report as complete. If the reference appears unjustified, raise an objection in the written opinion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amended claims / incorporated missing parts — general rule
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no right to amend the application until after the international search has been established; the search must be carried out on the transmitted search copy except for permitted corrections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Obvious mistakes or formal matters contrary to the PCT called to the applicant's attention by the RO may be corrected (GL/PCT-EPO H-IV). Substantive amendments (reformulation of claims, deletion/limitation of claims, taking subject-matter from description into claims) must be refused at this stage even if called 'corrections'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for rectification of obvious mistakes (Rule 91)
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant can request authorisation to rectify obvious mistakes; examiner must assess whether the request can be authorised according to Rule 91 criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See GL/ISPE 8.07-8.08 and GL/PCT-EPO H-IV,2. If RO erroneously authorised such rectification, this may affect the search. Refuse requests that are substantive amendments rather than true corrections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporating missing parts/elements contained in priority document
rubrics_metrics.description: If missing parts or an entire element of the application were completely contained in the priority document, they may be furnished later without affecting the international filing date, subject to Rules 4.18 and 20.6(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examiner checks whether the RO's assessment of 'completely contained' was correct (GL/PCT-EPO H-II,2.2.2). If RO erroneously considered them contained, extend the search to include documents relevant if the application were to be redated; cite such documents as 'L' in the ISR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anticipation of amendments to claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Anticipate possible amendments to claims when planning/searching.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply Section B-III, 3.5 of the Guidelines for Examination in the EPO mutatis mutandis (GL/ISPE 15.25). Consider how likely amendments could affect search scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Broad claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Special considerations apply when claims are broad.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply Section B-III, 3.6 of the EPO Guidelines mutatis mutandis (GL/ISPE 15.26). Take care to search the breadth that is meaningfully defined.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independent and dependent claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Search considerations differ for independent vs dependent claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply Section B-III, 3.7 of the Guidelines mutatis mutandis (GL/ISPE 15.27). Ensure dependent claims are assessed appropriately in the search plan.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search on dependent claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Dependent claims should be searched as set out in the Guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply Section B-III, 3.8 mutatis mutandis. See also GL/PCT-EPO F-IV, 3.3 and GL/ISPE 15.28.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combination of elements in a claim
rubrics_metrics.description: Examine and search for combinations of claim elements appropriately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply Section B-III, 3.9 of the Guidelines mutatis mutandis (GL/ISPE 15.31). Consider likely combinations when selecting prior art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Different categories of subject-matter
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims of different categories (e.g., product, process, use) require appropriate search handling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply Section B-III, 3.10 mutatis mutandis (GL/ISPE 15.32). Tailor search sources and strategy to the claim category.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject-matter excluded from search
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner may exclude certain subject-matter from the search where the EPO as ISA is not required to deal with it or where lack of clarity/support prevents meaningful search.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exclude subject-matter under Art.17(2)(a) and Rule 39 when appropriate (GL/ISPE 15.33). If clarity/support of description/claims/drawings is so deficient that no meaningful search can be carried out, indicate exclusion and reasons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nucleotide and amino acid sequence listings
rubrics_metrics.description: If required electronic sequence listings are not furnished and late-fee not paid, ISA will search without the sequence listing to the extent a meaningful search can be carried out.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow Rule 5.2, 13ter.1 and OJ EPO guidance. See GL/PCT-EPO B-VIII,3.2 and GL/ISPE 9.39, 15.12. Note consequences for completeness of search.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lack of unity of invention (search-stage handling)
rubrics_metrics.description: When claims do not relate to one invention or a linked group forming a single inventive concept, invite applicant to pay additional search fees; if not paid, restrict search to first-mentioned invention(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow Art.17(3)(a) and GL/ISPE 15.24. Use Form PCT/ISA/206 to give complete and self-contained reasoning. Refund rules apply for doublures; see GL/PCT-EPO B-VII.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technological background
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider technological background in the search.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply Section B-III, 3.13 of the Guidelines for Examination in the EPO mutatis mutandis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analysis before searching — taking into account earlier searches and classification
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners may take earlier searches into account where appropriate; earlier EPO searches can reduce search effort and may trigger partial/full refund of search fee for 'doublures'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rules 4.12, 12bis, 23bis.1 and 41.1 govern requests. If earlier search not by EPO, examiner still does independent full-scope search; documents from earlier reports may be useful but no refund for non-EPO earlier searches. For applications filed on/after 1 July 2017, EPO ISA may take earlier search/classification into account when requested under Rule 4.12 or under Rule 41.2 (see OJ EPO 2014, A30; 2017, A21).

rubrics_metrics.name: PCT Direct processing and informal comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Under PCT Direct, applicants claiming priority from an earlier application searched by the EPO may file a PCT Direct letter with informal comments aimed at overcoming earlier search objections; examiner may take these into account.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requirements: (a) informal comments filed with RO in specified form, (b) international application claims priority of an earlier application searched by EPO. PCT Direct letters must be self-contained and submitted as a separate PDF document titled 'PCT Direct/informal comments', include marked-up differences if claims/description differ, and be filed in the ways specified. Examiner will acknowledge and address PCT Direct content in the written opinion provided the requirements are met; explicit reference to earlier search opinion only if annexed. PCT Direct letters become public on PATENTSCOPE.

rubrics_metrics.name: Third-party observations
rubrics_metrics.description: Third-party observations under the PCT should refer to novelty or inventive step; examiner should consider them similarly to the European procedure if forwarded before final report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See GL/PCT-EPO E-II and PCT AI Part 8. If observations are relevant, cite the documents in the ISR and Section V of WO-ISA. If observations are irrelevant or not understandable, do not include them in ISR and insert comment in Section V of WO-ISA explaining reasons. Third-party observations normally will not reach examiner if ISR established on time (before publication), but may do so if search is after an A2 publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documents cited in the application
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider documents cited by applicant when planning the search.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See ISPE Guidelines 15.37. Use applicant-cited documents as potential leads and check their relevance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search strategy: formulation and execution
rubrics_metrics.description: Formulate a search strategy, carry out the search covering types of documents, reformulate subject where necessary, and determine end of search per Guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply Sections B-IV, 2.2–2.6 of the EPO Guidelines mutatis mutandis: formulate search strategy (2.2), carry out search and consider types of documents (2.3), reformulate subject if needed (2.4), identify closest prior art and its effects (2.5), and determine end of search (2.6). Follow Art.18, Rule 43.5 and GL/ISPE 15.67, 15.69, 15.72 for end-of-search criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparation of the search report and corrections
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare ISR in accordance with procedures; if an error is found, consider issuing a corrected ISR (and possibly WO-ISA).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply Section B-IV, 3.1 mutatis mutandis. Consider reasons for amending the ISR (see ISPE Guidelines 15.74) and follow procedures for corrected ISR/WO-ISA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preclassification and IPC classification
rubrics_metrics.description: Preclassify and IPC-classify international applications for file routing and distribution; verify and amend classification as needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply Section B-V mutatis mutandis. Handle incorrect preclassification (B-V,2.1). For amended classification of late published search reports see ISPE 7.05. For IPC when scope unclear or lack of unity, follow B-V,3.2–3.3 and verify classification as in B-V,3.4 (GL/ISPE 7.02–7.08,15.39).

rubrics_metrics.name: State of the art — oral/non-written disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: Oral disclosure, use, exhibition, etc. are prior art only when substantiated by a written disclosure under PCT Rules (contrary to Art.54 EPC).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow Rules 33.1(a),(b) and ISPE Guidelines 11.22 and 15.05. If a non-written disclosure has a subsequently published written account before the relevant date, cite the written account and give its date. If non-written disclosure is not followed by any written account, it is not cited in ISR but a note is made and reconsidered if application enters European phase.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflicting applications and completion of search
rubrics_metrics.description: Potentially conflicting European and international applications may not be fully discoverable if ISR concluded less than 18 months after filing; complete search during mandatory top-up search or at examination stage if entering European phase.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See GL/PCT-EPO C-IV,5 and GL/EPO C-IV,7.1. Examiners should be aware of timing limitations and complete searches where required during top-up or examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verification of claimed priority date(s) and dates for cited documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Verify claimed priority dates and use correct date references for documents cited in the search report; handle intermediate documents and doubts per Guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply Section B-VI,5.1–5.3 mutatis mutandis (GL/ISPE 11.02–11.06). Consider documents published after the filing date and Rule 51bis.1(a)(v), Art.55 EPC. Extend search if doubts as to priority validity require redating.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-prejudicial disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: Potentially non-prejudicial disclosures should be cited in the ISR; whether they fall within Art.55(1)(a) or (b) EPC will be investigated at European phase.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See ISPE Guidelines 16.76. Cite such disclosures and flag them for later investigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Matters of doubt in the state of the art
rubrics_metrics.description: If there are uncertainties regarding the state of the art, handle them according to Guidelines and note them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply Section B-VI,5.6 mutatis mutandis; see ISPE Guidelines 11.23 and 15.64–15.65. Document doubts in the WO-ISA/ISR as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents of prior-art disclosures and handling problematic disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: Deal with issues such as documents not available/published in official EPO languages, conflicts between abstracts and source documents, insufficient prior-art disclosures, incorrect database records, and internet disclosures in technical journals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply Section B-VI,6 and its subsections mutatis mutandis (GL/ISPE references given). If source document conflicts with abstract, follow B-VI,6.3. For insufficient disclosures or incorrect records, follow B-VI,6.4–6.5. For internet disclosures in technical journals see B-VI,7 and ISPE 11.13.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unity of invention — Form 206 reasoning and applicant options
rubrics_metrics.description: When lack of unity is found at search stage, the examiner must complete Form PCT/ISA/206 giving complete reasoning; applicant may (i) not pay, (ii) pay without protest, or (iii) pay under protest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow Art.17(3)(a), Rule 13, 40.1 and GL/ISPE 10. On issuance, send WO-ISA and Form 206 together. Refund and doublure rules apply; see OJ EPO 2017, A20.

rubrics_metrics.name: No request for payment of additional search fees (exception)
rubrics_metrics.description: In exceptional cases the examiner may choose not to request additional search fees even if lack of unity objection occurs (e.g., additional effort minor).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If chosen, ISR is issued for all inventions indicating lack of unity; WO-ISA completed for all searched inventions and Section IV explains non-unity with full reasons. Examiner should consider consistency with potential later examination fees and the whole procedure's examination effort (see GL/PCT-EPO C-V,3.3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Cascading non-unity
rubrics_metrics.description: If additional search fees are paid and further lack of unity is discovered 'a posteriori' during additional search, no further invitation for fees is issued; only first invention of each subgroup is searched.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adapt WO-ISA Sections III–V to reflect inventions actually searched; provide full reasons in Section IV and opinions on searched inventions in Section V. Claims not searched in international phase can be prosecuted in regional phase before EPO (GL/EPO F-V,13.1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Documents relevant only to other inventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Handle documents that are relevant only to inventions other than those searched per EPO Guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply provisions of section B-VII,1.3 of the Guidelines for Examination in the EPO mutatis mutandis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reply to invitation to pay additional search fees — no payment
rubrics_metrics.description: If applicant does not pay additional search fees after invitation, final search report and WO-ISA already prepared are sent out by formalities officer; file not returned to examiner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow GL/PCT-EPO B-VII procedures. Ensure ISR and WO-ISA reflect inventions searched initially.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reply to invitation — payment without protest
rubrics_metrics.description: If applicant pays additional search fees without protest, a complete search is carried out for inventions for which fees were paid and ISR/WO-ISA drafted accordingly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Modify Section III to reflect actual payment; fill out Section IV and give opinions under Section V for searched inventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reply to invitation — payment under protest and Review Panel outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: If applicant pays under protest, protest procedure is triggered; outcomes of Review Panel determine whether ISR/WO-ISA must be adapted (e.g., add/remove non-unity indication, adapt reasoning and opinions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow Rule 40.2(c) and GL/ISPE 10.66–10.69. If protest fully or partly justified, adapt ISR/WO-ISA to Review Panel decision. If protest fully justified and application considered unitary, send final ISR with no non-unity indication; adapt WO-ISA Section IV accordingly. If protest not justified, indicate non-unity in ISR and WO-ISA Section IV and proceed for paid inventions. Send final ISR/WO-ISA together with decision on protest (Form PCT/ISA/212) to ensure consistency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protest procedure — admissibility requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Before initiating protest procedure, check formal admissibility under Rule 40.2(c); protest must satisfy requirements including payment of prescribed protest fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Initial review by formalities officer then Review Panel within ISA. Ensure applicant has paid prescribed protest fee (Rule 40.2(e)) and other admissibility checks are met before proceeding.
